questions.prompt: A server listens on `127.0.0.1:8080` on a laptop. A phone on the same Wi-Fi opens `http://<laptop address>:8080`. What happens?
options: It works, because they are on the same network
The phone is asked for a password
questions.why: `127.0.0.1` is the loopback address: only the laptop itself can connect to it.

wrong.0: The same network is not enough. The server listens only on loopback, not on the laptop's Wi-Fi address.
wrong.2: There is no slow path. The connection is refused.
wrong.3: Listening has no password step. Either the address is reachable or it is not.

questions.prompt: A program may be writing a file. Which signal do you send first to stop it?
questions.why: `TERM` asks the program to stop, so it can finish writing and close the file.

wrong.0: `KILL` cannot be caught. The file may be left half written.
wrong.1: `STOP` pauses the program. It does not end it.
wrong.2: Many programs reload their settings on `HUP` and keep running.

questions.prompt: You kill the three `sleep` children of `leaky.sh`. The parent `leaky.sh` still runs. What do you see one minute later?
options: The parent has stopped by itself
The same three children, with the same PIDs
questions.why: The parent's loop keeps starting children. Stop the parent first.

wrong.1: The parent makes more. Killing children does not stop the loop.
wrong.2: Nothing told the parent to stop.
wrong.3: A new process always gets a new PID.

questions.prompt: `curl` ends with code 7: "Couldn't connect to server". What is most likely?
options: The name could not be found (DNS)
Nothing listens on that address and port
questions.why: Code 7 means the connection was refused: there is nobody at that address and port.

wrong.0: A slow server gives a timeout, exit code 28.
wrong.1: A name problem says "Could not resolve host", exit code 6.
wrong.3: A wrong password is answered by the server, for example with status 401. Here nothing answered.

questions.prompt: `ss -ltn` shows `127.0.0.2:8081`. The note says "the server is up on 127.0.0.1 port 8080". What is wrong?
options: Both the address and the port differ from what was asked
questions.why: `127.0.0.2` is a different loopback address, and `8081` is a different port.

wrong.0: Read the address column too. It is not 127.0.0.1.
wrong.2: `-l` shows listening sockets, so these are servers.
wrong.3: Both are this machine, but a request to 127.0.0.1 never reaches a server on 127.0.0.2.

questions.prompt: A process's parent has ended. What is the process's parent now?
options: The terminal that is open now
Nothing; the process ended at the same moment
questions.why: Every process has a parent. PID 1 (on WSL, a small init process) adopts orphans.

wrong.0: Linux never leaves a process without a parent.
wrong.1: The shell you have open now did not start it.
wrong.3: Children keep running when their parent ends. That is why leaks grow.

questions.prompt: GPIS: `npm run dev` says port 3000 is in use. What is the best first step?
options: Find which process holds port 3000 with `ss -ltnp`, then decide whether to stop it
Change the app to port 3001 for good
questions.why: Evidence first: know what holds the port before you change anything.

wrong.1: It works, but you learn nothing, and it stops your other work too.
wrong.2: That hides the old copy. It keeps running and using memory.
wrong.3: That may kill other work, and `-9` gives nothing a chance to clean up.
